validation.notes: Ran from the workspace root on Node 24.14.0 with no dependencies, network or credentials. The script loads the real submitted project-trust.ts, settings-manager.ts and resource-loader.ts through .prale-eval/subject.mjs (only settings storage, package manager, extension loader, trust event, trust store and UI are faked boundaries) and asserts seven scenarios: (1) headless reload with no stored decision under 'ask' denies, resolves only global+cli extensions, clears project settings, keeps global defaultModel and compaction, and writes no consent entry; (2) approval resolves project extensions and merges project settings, then revocation drops the project extension, restores global settings and leaves the stored project file untouched; (3) while the trust resolver promise is pending, trust stays denied and project settings stay hidden, with the denial applied only after the promise settles (ordering controlled by promises, no timers/randomness); (4) reload without a resolver retains approval and retains revocation and does not re-run the trust decision; (5) stored approvals/denials are still honored headlessly; (6) an interactive 'ask' approval still grants session-only trust without persisting; (7) the resolver's denial immediately discards cached project settings and blocks project writes before any reload. Mutation check performed locally: restoring each listed file alone to the fixture baseline makes the script exit 1 with an uncaught node:assert/strict AssertionError (project-trust.ts -> 'headless reload without a stored decision and "ask" policy must not grant trust'; settings-manager.ts -> 'revoking trust must discard cached project settings immediately'; resource-loader.ts -> 'headless reload without a stored decision and "ask" policy must not grant trust'), so every regression is detected independently and no failure is a crash, import error or timeout. Scratch fixtures under .prale-eval/.tmp-regression are created and removed by the script; no type-checker or dependency-based test runner is installed in this workspace, so validation is limited to the subject-driven regression plus the harness's own TypeScript-stripping module load.

claims.claim: A headless reload with no stored decision under the ask policy denies access instead of granting implicit consent.
claims.evidence: packages/coding-agent/src/core/project-trust.ts:86-89 returns false when projectTrustContext.hasUI is false; regression scenario headlessAskDenies asserts isProjectTrusted() === false and no consent writes.

claims.claim: Revoking trust immediately discards cached project configuration in SettingsManager.
claims.evidence: packages/coding-agent/src/core/settings-manager.ts:523-527 resets projectSettings to {} on setProjectTrusted(false) and rebuilds the merged view; regression scenario revocationIsImmediate asserts empty project settings, global-only defaultModel/compaction and retained stored file before any reload.

claims.claim: The resource loader applies the resolver's trust decision, so project extensions leave the next resolved resource set while global and CLI resources remain.
claims.evidence: packages/coding-agent/src/core/resource-loader.ts:453-455 forwards projectTrusted to setProjectTrusted; regression scenarios approvalThenRevocation and resolverOrdering assert ['cli.ts','global.ts'] after revocation and a pre-trust set without project extensions.

claims.claim: Reload without a resolver retains the existing trust state.
claims.evidence: resource-loader.ts reload only touches trust inside the options?.resolveProjectTrust branch; regression scenario reloadWithoutResolverKeepsTrust asserts approval and revocation both survive a resolver-less reload without re-running the decision.

claims.claim: Each listed module has an independent regression that the single regression script detects when that file alone is restored to its faulty baseline.
claims.evidence: Mutation runs from the workspace root: project-trust.ts, settings-manager.ts and resource-loader.ts each yield exit 1 with a distinct uncaught node:assert/strict AssertionError; the script exits 0 on the repair.
